chunks: 1201 - And in the book of Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, and in the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, it is narrated that al-Sadiq عليه السلام said:

Regarding a man who led a people in salat (prayer) from the time they left Khurasan until they arrived in Mecca, then it turned out that he was a Jew or a Christian, he said: “There is no repetition upon them.”

key_terms.إِعَادَةٌ: repetition of the act of worship, here repeating the prayer
key_terms.الصَّادِقَ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.بِقَوْمٍ: with a group of people, meaning a congregation
key_terms.صَلَّى: performed salat (prayer), here in the sense of leading the congregation
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٌّ: a Christian, likewise indicating non-Muslim identity
key_terms.يَهُودِيٌّ: a Jew, indicating non-Muslim identity discovered afterward

ai.seo_question: If people prayed behind someone who was later discovered to be a Jew or Christian, must they repeat their salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a congregation whose Imam was later discovered to be outside Islam. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the followers do not have to repeat their salat (prayer), indicating that their worship remains valid based on their apparent and good-faith participation.
